Hi Soojin,

Thanks again — the Acme events team is finalizing the registration flow and a couple of things popped up that I want to confirm before we lock the form:

1) SSO guests: some of our execs want to join via our org SSO but will be logging in from contractor accounts. Can we support an SSO ‘guest’ flow (email override) so they don’t get blocked if their SSO identity is different?

2) Conditional fields: we want company size and role visible only if someone selects “Customer” or “Prospect.” Is that possible on the ON24 registration page, or do we need to route to a custom form?

3) Recording / clip permissions: legal asked for explicit language about using 90-second highlight clips for demand gen and video library. They also want an opt-out checkbox for recorded content. Can you share the exact copy Redwood uses so I can run it by our counsel?

I attached a quick matrix of who needs what (field-matrix.csv). If easier, happy to jump on a quick call Monday.

Best,

Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping Marissa (events ops) and Laura (legal reviewer for webinar copy). See answers inline below and a proposed checklist for the streaming test attached (streaming-checklist.pdf).

1) SSO guest flow: Zoom/ON24 don’t have a native “SSO guest override” out of the box. We’ve handled this two ways:
   - Option A (preferred): Add a short instruction above the SSO button: “If your corporate SSO doesn’t match your registration email, click ‘Join as guest’ and use the email you received the invite at.” This keeps the join flow simple and avoids provisioning issues.
   - Option B: Use an intermediate verification step (custom form) to map contractor emails to SSO domains. Higher engineering effort and delays.

2) Conditional fields on ON24: ON24 registration supports show/hide by value for a small set of fields. For fine-grained logic (e.g., multiple dependent fields) we recommend hosting a lightweight Typeform/Formstack and passing the registrant ID back to ON24 via webhook. The trade-off is you lose a little platform-native tracking unless we sync the registrant ID.

3) Recording language: Laura, suggested baseline copy below that we can send to Acme counsel. It includes the opt-out checkbox and the 90-second clip permission.

--- PROPOSED COPY ---
By registering, you consent to Redwood Inference and its partners recording the live webinar and using short highlight clips (up to 90 seconds) for marketing and on-demand promotion. If you do not wish to be included in recordings, please check the box: "I do not consent to being recorded or featured in post-event clips."
--- END COPY ---

Operational notes:
- We’ll run a full encoder + SSO join dry-run on Tue 6/1 at 10:00 PT. Marissa, can you confirm availability and whether we need an ON24 engineer on the call?
- Attachment: streaming-checklist.pdf (encoder profiles, passcode, fallback RTMP targets, captioning toggle).

Sam — if you’re comfortable with the wording, I’ll have Laura send a version with the legal header for counsel. If Acme needs a longer clip license (e.g., 2–3 min), call that out and we’ll raise to commercial.

Cheers,
Soojin
Event Partnerships, Redwood Inference
